scope: 14 training workloads; three fresh CPU and MPS processes each; six separate memory diagnostics

methodology.order: Alternate CPU/MPS order within each case and reverse starting order between cases; all workers serialized
methodology.timing: Warm runtime; fresh matrices; training includes quantization and per-round evaluation; loading, matrix setup and final prediction excluded
methodology.conditions: AC power at pre/post-run checks; other applications, temperature and system paging not controlled; no overlapping project builds or tests
methodology.gpu_readings: IORegistry driver utilization snapshots outside worker timing; not a calibrated measure of GPU occupancy or an attribution to another application
methodology.correctness: Exact same-device repeated model bytes, margins and every-round metrics; exact CPU inference of each MPS model checked outside timing; independent CPU/MPS models may differ
methodology.published_wrapper: The unchanged published worker is followed by saved-model CPU inference and library/model hashes; wrapper outside timed training

fresh_cpu_prediction_validation.method: Reload each saved model into a new CPU Booster with an empty prediction cache; reconstruct and fingerprint original held-out data; no training

postmeasurement_prediction_check_fixes.description: Changing device can reuse cached predictions. Both benchmark drivers now reload saved MPS models into new CPU Boosters for prediction checks. These changes are after timed training; all measured models were validated independently with fresh CPU predictors.
